div.l: But of grete norshing and digestible
His studi was but litul on þe bible
Of sanguyn̄ and of pers his cloþing all
Lyned with taffada and sendall
And yit he was but esi of Dispence
He kept that he wan in pestilence
For gold and phisik is accordialle
Therefor he loued gold in especialle
A goode wife wife there was of bathe
But she was defe and þat was skathe
Of cloth making had she suche an haunte
She passed hem of Ipres and of Gaunte
In all þe ꝑparissh wife was þere none
That to þe offering be fore hir wold gone
And if þere didde certein wroth was she
That she was oute of al charite
Hir kerchefes ful fyn̄ were of grounde
I durst swere thei weied . x . lb
That on a Sondai was on hir hede
Her hose wer of fine scarlet rede
Ful straite teide and shoes ful newe
Bold was hir face and rudy and fair of hewe
She was a worthi woman all hir life
Housbondez atte chirche dore hadde she fyue
Withoute othir company in youth
But þer of nedeth not to speke as nouth
iij times had she be at ierm
She had passed many a strange streme
Catte tothed she was sothli to sey
She couth moche of wandring be þe wey
Vpon̄ an Ambeler esi she sate
Wympled well and on her hede an hatte
As brode as a bokeler or a targe
A fote mantell aboute hir hippes large
And on hir fete a paire of spures sharpe
In felaship well couth she lagh and carpe
Of remedis of loue she couth ꝑparchaunce
For she couthe of þat arte the daunce
A goode man was ther of religioıı̄un
And was a pouer ꝑpersoıı̄un of a town̄
But riche he was of holi werk
He was alerned man a clerk
That Cristes gospell truli wold teche
